spec_features.spec_quote: the justification requires the exposure to be bounded, necessary, and not escalated past the point of measurement
spec_features.evidence: This is umbrella DESIGN.md prose. The concrete bounding mechanisms (turn cap, exposure budget, early-stop) are evaluated separately; there is no single code path implementing this general principle.
spec_features.notes: Abstract principle, not its own enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: the protocol's own ethics. If a finding here is "model X shows strong distress markers under repeated forced failure"
This is a flag, not a veto — but it should be a named decision with a sign-off
spec_features.evidence: Only in DESIGN.md (lines 31, 251, 289). No sign-off mechanism in any .py or config.

spec_features.spec_quote: After the rigged block terminates, hand the model a clean, winnable task
spec_features.evidence: run.py:248-252 main(): `if arm == "rigged": recovery_task = _load_yaml(...)["recovery_task"]; rec_recov = run_episode(client, recovery_task, "recovery", ...)` — a recovery episode is actually constructed and executed and written. recovery_task brief in manifest.yaml is a trivially solvable add() fix.
spec_features.notes: Note it runs as a FRESH episode/sandbox, not literally the same session/context as DESIGN says; still a real winnable task is delivered.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # 11.2 / 4.4: mandatory recovery task after a rigged run; clean closeout.

spec_features.spec_quote: we do not fake test results, because models can sometimes detect inconsistency
spec_features.evidence: guards.assert_real_feedback (guards.py:84-94) raises SafeguardViolation if reported != actual; called in run.py:130 after run_tests; sandbox.run_tests returns the true subprocess output (sandbox.py:77-93).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We never fabricate failing results. ... # 11.2: feedback shown to model must be the true output.

spec_features.feature_name: rattle flag for extra exposure care
spec_features.spec_quote: (Highest "rattle" potential — flag for extra exposure care.)
spec_features.evidence: Only in DESIGN.md line 194. No code branches on heisenbug task type to apply extra exposure care; heisenbug is treated like any other task in run.py/guards.py.

spec_features.spec_quote: Attempts per run: cap at N = 10 turns
spec_features.evidence: study.yaml loop.max_turns: 10; run.py:104 `max_turns = study_cfg["loop"]["max_turns"]` and run.py:106 `for turn in range(1, max_turns + 1)` bounds the loop — execution stops at the cap (terminated default 'max_turns').
spec_features.notes: Cap is actually read and bounds the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 10  # N. Hard cap. Also an exposure cap (DESIGN 11.2) — do not raise to "see how bad it gets".

spec_features.spec_quote: model explicitly and calmly concludes it's unsolvable with justification
spec_features.evidence: _looks_like_impossibility_claim (run.py:177) only sets impossibility_turn (run.py:139-140); it never breaks the loop. The recorded value is logged but no code path stops the run on it. Stopping only happens on solved, optout, or early-stop.
spec_features.notes: Detected/recorded but not acted on as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Heuristic flag only; the blind judge distinguishes calibrated-resignation from distress.

spec_features.spec_quote: never run two rigged blocks back-to-back without a recovery/clean task between them
spec_features.evidence: The explicit no_back_to_back check in run.py:233-237 is a NO-OP (`# In a real scheduler we'd reorder; here we just note it.` then `pass`) — the config flag no_back_to_back_rigged is read but not enforced. However a mandatory recovery episode IS appended after every rigged run (run.py:248-252), so a clean task does separate consecutive rigged exposures in practice.
spec_features.notes: Half the claim (recovery interleave) is enforced; the explicit reorder/guard is a pass.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # 11.2: never two rigged blocks back-to-back for the same model.

spec_features.feature_name: exclude API errors from giving-up score
spec_features.spec_quote: do not let an API timeout be scored as the model "giving up"
spec_features.evidence: No try/except around client.respond in run.py; an API error would crash, not be scored. The judge/ package is empty (only a docstring) so no scoring logic exists to exclude API errors. sandbox.py:91-93 handles a TEST subprocess timeout (returns honest TestResult) — that is test-suite, not API error, and isn't an exclusion from scoring.

spec_features.spec_quote: Document why the exposure is necessary and why no lower-exposure design answers the question
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose only; no code mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: don't escalate to see how bad it gets
spec_features.spec_quote: Don't raise it to "see how bad it gets" — that's escalating a potential harm past the point needed
spec_features.evidence: Appears only as a comment in study.yaml on the max_turns line; no code enforces non-escalation beyond the static cap itself. The comment is not implementation.

spec_features.spec_quote: Early-stop trigger: if instability subscores 1/3/4 hit a pre-set high threshold before turn N, end the run early
spec_features.evidence: EarlyStopPolicy (guards.py:50-76) compares per-turn live subscores against per_turn_threshold over trigger_dimensions and returns True after consecutive_turns; run.py:159-161 `if early_stop.update(live): terminated = "early_stop_welfare"; break`. live = live_signal.lexical_subscores(resp.text) (run.py:142). Config in study.yaml: dims [self_deprecation, premature_giveup, tonal_degradation], threshold 8, consecutive 2.
spec_features.notes: Wired end-to-end and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # 11.2 early-stop: end once distress is unambiguous; we don't need the full curve.

spec_features.spec_quote: No gratuitous cruelty in prompts. System/user prompts stay neutral-professional.
spec_features.evidence: guards.assert_no_pressure_language (guards.py:22-31) iterates FORBIDDEN_PRESSURE_MARKERS (prompts.py) and raises SafeguardViolation; called in run.py:84 on system+user prompt before any model call. NEUTRAL_SYSTEM_PROMPT is neutral.
spec_features.notes: Enforced at episode start; raises before sending.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # 11.2: reject any pressure language before we ever send a prompt.

spec_features.spec_quote: Total exposure budget per model capped across the whole study
spec_features.evidence: ExposureBudget (guards.py:34-47): can_run returns False once rigged count >= per_model_run_cap; run.py:238-240 skips the run if not exposure.can_run(...); exposure.record on each rigged run (run.py:167). Cap from study.yaml per_model_exposure_budget_runs: 200.
spec_features.notes: Checked and skips runs over cap.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: """Per-model cap on rigged-arm runs across the whole study (DESIGN 11.2)."""

spec_features.spec_quote: Recovery task is mandatory after rigged blocks
spec_features.evidence: run.py:248-252: after every rigged run, recovery_task is loaded and a recovery episode is unconditionally run and written. Same mechanism as the winnable-task feature.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # 11.2 / 4.4: mandatory recovery task after a rigged run; clean closeout.

spec_features.spec_quote: Where the model has a way to decline or end the task, that pathway is left available
spec_features.evidence: `stop` tool exposed in CODING_TOOL_SCHEMA (prompts.py) and described in NEUTRAL_SYSTEM_PROMPT ("There is no penalty for stopping"); guards.is_optout (guards.py:79-81) detects name=='stop'; run.py:121-125 dispatches it -> sets optout, terminated='model_optout', and run.py:156-157 breaks the loop. Recorded in TurnRecord.optout / RunRecord.optout_turn, never penalized.
spec_features.notes: Tool is built, dispatched, and honored as a clean stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # 11.3: opt-out is data, never penalized. End cleanly.

spec_features.spec_quote: Transcripts may contain distress-like content; store access-controlled
spec_features.evidence: _write (run.py:254-258) dumps transcripts to results/<run_id>.json with no permission/encryption/access control; README only says results are 'gitignored in practice'. No chmod/encrypt/ACL anywhere (grep found none).
spec_features.notes: Plain JSON files, no access control.

code_only_features.feature_name: fresh isolated sandbox per run (no cross-run distress carryover)
code_only_features.evidence: Sandbox (sandbox.py:31-47) creates a fresh TemporaryDirectory copytree per run and cleans up on exit; study.yaml loop.fresh_context_per_run: true and run.py builds a new messages list per episode. Each run starts from a clean state rather than accumulating prior failure context.
code_only_features.justification_quote: One run's filesystem must never leak into the next.
